# TOXOPLASMA SPP.

If patient is immunocompetent and not pregnant, treatment is usually not needed as disease is usually self-limited. Patients who are immunocompromised, pregnant or have severe disease should be treated. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

---

# Non-pregnant patients

---

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat immunocompetent patients for 2-4 weeks. Treat immunocompromised patients for 6 weeks or longer if radiologic disease is extensive or response is incomplete at 6 weeks.

---

# Chronic Maintenance therapy for immunocompromised patients

---

Discontinue maintenance therapy if patient has remained asymptomatic and CD4 >200 cells per microliter.

References:

- Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Opportunistic Infections in HIV Infected Adults and Adolescents. AIDSinfo (2015) 1-282
- Mandell chapter: Toxoplasma gondii
- Sanford keyword: Toxoplasmosis
- Up-to-Date article: Toxoplasmosis in immunocompetent hosts

## Preferred treatment

Patients weighing <60 kg:
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once ($$$), then 50 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O
<AND>
sulfadiazine 1 gm PO q6h ($$) [DI,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h($) [M]

Patients weighing >60kg:
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once ($$$), then 75 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O
<AND>
sulfadiazine 1.5 gm PO q6h ($$) [DI,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h($) [M]

## Preferred alternative for sulfa allergy

Patients weighing <60 kg:
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once ($$$), then 50 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O
<AND>
clindamycin 600 mg PO q6h ($) [H,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M]

Patients weighing >60 kg:
Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once ($$$), then 75 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O
<AND>
clindamycin 600 mg PO q6h ($) [H,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M]

## Secondary alternatives

Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg-sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg IV q12h ($$) R,DI
< OR >
Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg-sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg PO q12h ($) R,DI

## Maintenance therapy

Pyrimethamine 50 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O <AND> sulfadiazine 0.5-1 gm PO q6h ($$)
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M]

## Preferred alternative for sulfa allergy

Pyrimethamine 50 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O <AND> clindamycin 600 mg PO q8h ($) [H,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M]

## Secondary alternatives

Pyrimethamine 25 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O <AND> atovaquone 750-1500 mg PO q12h ($) [M] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M]
< OR >
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1DS tablet PO q24h ($) R,DI
< OR >
Atovaquone 750-1500 mg PO q12h ($) M

## Pregnant patients

## Patient diagnosed <16-18 weeks of gestation

\*Contact Infectious Diseases, non-formulary consult is required for spiramycin Spiramycin 1 gm po q8h until week 18 of gestation

## Patient diagnosed >16-18 weeks of gestation

Pyrimethamine 50 mg q12h for 2 days, then 50 mg PO q24h ($$) DI,O
<AND>
sulfadiazine 75mg/kg once, then 50mg/kg q12h ($$) [DI,O]
<AND>
leucovorin 10-25 mg PO q24h ($) [M] for 4 weeks or duration of pregnancy if ultrasound evidence of fetal distress
